project.name: openCG
project.tagline: A self-hostable context pipeline that exposes a private knowledge catalogue to any AI tool over MCP, and logs every byte it hands over.

pillars.title: Ingestion
pillars.tagline: The front door. Turns a git repo into searchable pieces.
pillars.what:
The front door of the whole system. You hand it a git repository URL and it walks every file, decides what is worth indexing, and feeds each file into the rest of the pipeline.

Nothing else in openCG does anything useful until content has come through here.
pillars.why: A retrieval system is only as good as what it has read. Ingestion is the part that does the reading, and it is deliberately conservative: it would rather skip a file it cannot handle cleanly than store garbage that pollutes search results forever.

flow.title: Trigger a run
flow.detail: Either the CLI (opencg-ingest git <repo_url>) or the HTTP API (POST /run/git on port 8100). The HTTP route queues the work with FastAPI BackgroundTasks and returns immediately with status: "queued", so the admin UI does not block on a long clone.

flow.title: Shallow-clone the repository
flow.detail: git clone --depth 1 into a temporary directory, then git rev-parse HEAD to record the exact commit. That SHA is stored on every row the run produces, so you can always answer "which version of the repo did this text come from".

flow.title: Discover the files worth indexing
flow.detail: Two discovery passes are merged. graphifyy identifies real source code across roughly 80 extensions and 28 tree-sitter languages. A manual extension list catches prose and config: .md, .markdown, .rst, .txt, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .json, .ini, .html, .css, .scss, .sass. If a path appears in both passes, the code path wins.

flow.title: Filter out what cannot be handled
flow.detail: Anything larger than 1 MB is skipped. Anything that is not valid UTF-8 is skipped. Binaries and unrecognised extensions never enter the list at all, and graphifyy honours the repo's own .graphifyignore plus the usual noise directories like node_modules.

flow.title: Build a stable document identity
flow.detail: Each surviving file becomes a document with a SHA-256 hash of its raw bytes and a deterministic UUID derived from {tenant}:{source_uri}. Because the ID is derived rather than random, re-ingesting the same file always lands on the same row instead of creating a duplicate.

flow.title: Hand off to the per-document pipeline
flow.detail: For each document: write a parent row to the catalog, chunk the content, write a row per chunk, embed each chunk, upsert the vector, and run graph extraction. Those steps are covered by the Chunking, Model Providers, Vector Index, Catalog Store, and Knowledge Graph pillars.

flow.title: Record the run
flow.detail: Counts of documents and chunks land in an in-memory ring buffer of the last 100 runs, which is what /ingestion in the admin UI displays.

facts: Skips: non-UTF-8, binaries, unknown extensions, .graphifyignore matches
Readiness depends on Postgres, Qdrant, and Ollama all answering
opencg-ingest re-extract re-runs graph extraction on existing chunks without re-embedding
gaps: No PDFs, images, OCR, or file upload. The Confluence, web-indexer, and custom-API connectors are declared in GET /connectors but report themselves as deferred.
No unchanged-content short-circuit. content_hash is stored but never compared before work begins, so re-ingesting a repo re-chunks and re-embeds every file even if nothing changed.
Deleted files are never tombstoned. A file removed from the repo upstream stays in the catalog and in Qdrant indefinitely.
Run history is in-memory only. Restarting the container loses it; there is no persistent job queue, no retry, and no scheduler.

changes.name: fix-symbol-attribution
changes.why: `add-incremental-ingest` gives `chunk_code_by_symbols` a completeness contract: report `symbols` when every discovered symbol produced a chunk, and `partial` when any were lost. A `partial` file never earns a completion marker, so it is reprocessed on the next run rather than skipped — the safety property that stops the gate freezing a half-finished file.
what_changes: **Discovery is narrowed to the nodes the extractor attributed to the file being parsed**, before completeness is judged. A node is kept when its `source_file` resolves to the path handed to `graphify.extract`, and dropped otherwise. That excludes referenced types, whose `source_file` is empty because under single-file extraction their defining file is genuinely unknown, and import targets, whose `source_file` names a different file the extractor never read.

**A malformed definition is kept, not filtered.** A node attributed to this file stays in the discovered population however broken its other fields are, so failing to place it reports as `partial` rather than disappearing. This is why no discriminator-failure guard is needed: the failure mode reports itself.
**A file whose only AST nodes besides the module node were attributed elsewhere** takes the existing zero-symbol path and reports `no_symbols`, so its text is still chunked and searchable.

changes.name: bootstrap-thin-mvp
changes.why: The `add-foundation` change describes the v0 product — twelve capabilities, full 7-stage pipeline, four ingestion connectors, OPA enforcement, replay, full admin UI. That is the right destination but it is not what we can ship first. To prove the architecture works end-to-end we need a thinner slice that ingests something, retrieves it through the pipeline, returns context to an MCP client, and lands an audit row.
what_changes: **Formalize the thin-MVP scope cut** against `add-foundation`: MCP exposes one functional tool (`opencg/retrieve_for_context`); the pipeline runs four stages (identity → hybrid retrieval → assemble → return); ingestion is git-only; admin UI is one page plus a Storybook scaffold; deployment is dev-profile-only. The other v0 capabilities (`knowledge-graph`, full `model-providers` abstraction, intent classification, rerank+compress as separate stages, OPA enforcement, replay, additional connectors, full admin UI, Grafana dashboards, `local-prod` profile) are explicitly deferred to follow-up changes.

**Adopt a local Ollama service in docker-compose** as the embeddings backend for the thin MVP. The model is pulled on first start of the service. The service is reachable from `pipeline` and `ingestion` at `http://ollama:11434`. Ollama Cloud configuration stays in place (env-driven `base_url` + `api_key`) but is reserved for chat/generation in follow-up changes; the thin MVP does not call Cloud.

Document in `model-providers` that v0 embeddings require an Ollama-compatible host that exposes `/api/embeddings` (or `/api/embed`); Ollama Cloud's `/api/embed` is gated and MUST NOT be relied on as the embeddings backend until a future change introduces a separate provider for it.

changes.name: add-incremental-ingest
changes.why: Every git re-ingest re-chunks and re-embeds the entire repository. `content_hash` is computed for every file, written to the catalog, and never read back — the only reads are for admin display. Embedding is one sequential HTTP call per chunk, so a repo producing 45,000 chunks pays 45,000 round trips on every run, plus a second model call per prose chunk for graph extraction. Fixing one typo costs the same as the first ingest.
what_changes: **A completion marker replaces the hash as the skip key.** Stored in the parent entity's existing `metadata` JSONB under a namespaced, versioned key, it records the `content_hash` that completed, an `embedding_fingerprint` (provider, model, vector dimension), a `chunker_version` (graphifyy version plus an application-controlled chunker format version and its constants), an `extraction_version`, the `chunk_mode` that was actually used, `chunk_count`, and `completed_at`.

**A file is skipped only when the marker parses, is a known version, and every identity component matches.** Absent, malformed, unknown-version, or any mismatch means process normally. Absent fails open by design: no existing row has a marker, so the first run after this ships reprocesses the corpus once.

**The marker is earned, not assumed.** It is written only after every chunk of that file embedded and upserted without error, extraction was not degraded, the code graph persisted where one was expected, and the file was not truncated mid-flight. Truncation is judged **per file**, not per run.

**The chunker reports why it produced text chunks.** `chunk_code_by_symbols` currently returns plain text chunks from two different places — extraction raised, or the file genuinely has no symbols — with identical return shape. The second is spec-mandated correct behaviour. Without distinguishing them, either degraded files freeze forever or every symbol-free source file reprocesses forever. The function gains an explicit outcome so the marker can tell them apart.

**Marker publication is compare-and-set.** Nothing serialises ingests — every `POST /run/git` spawns a background task — so two runs of the same repo can interleave. The write is conditional on the row still belonging to the attempt that did the work.
**Skipped files are still touched.** A skip bypasses `insert_entity`, so a lightweight catalog method refreshes verification state without rewriting content.

**Markers are invalidatable.** Recreating Qdrant collections is a documented operator procedure, after which every marker still passes and nothing re-ingests. An explicit invalidation path prevents that trap.

**Runs report what they skipped.** `IngestionSummary`, `RunStore`, `GET /runs/recent`, and the admin ingestion page all carry a skipped count. This is a safety surface, not cosmetics: an over-aggressive gate is otherwise invisible.

changes.name: add-foundation
changes.why: General-purpose LLMs are trained on general-purpose knowledge. Enterprise standards, taxonomy, patterns, and policies are specific to each organization and never reach the training data. A single LLM tool RAG-ing against a vector database is one component — not an AI architecture.
what_changes: New service: **MCP server** (TypeScript) exposing `search`, `retrieve_for_context`, `get_entity`, `traverse_graph`, `submit_feedback` tools and a structured response contract.

New service: **Retrieval pipeline** — orchestrates the 7-stage runtime path (identity → intent classification → hybrid retrieval → catalog/graph enrichment → rerank+compress → entitlement+audit → structured return).
New service: **Background enrichment workers** — change-driven enrichment, freshness monitoring, relationship inference, usage-feedback streaming.
New service: **Ingestion connectors** — git, confluence, custom HTTP APIs, and a web-page indexer with allow-listed domains.
New service: **Admin UI** — query review, returned-context inspection, graph relationship management, vector neighbourhood exploration, content management, ingestion control.

New shared storage layer: **PostgreSQL** (Apache AGE for graph, `pg_trgm` and `tsvector` for BM25-style lexical), **Qdrant** (vector store with hybrid dense+sparse), **Valkey** (cache + session), **OPA sidecar** (policy engine).

New abstraction: **Model-provider adapters** — single interface for embeddings, intent classification, rerank, generation; first-class adapters for Ollama and Anthropic; OpenAI-compatible adapter for portability.
**Identity stub** — hardcoded principal + correlation ID in v0; auth is explicitly deferred but the propagation contract is established now so it can be swapped without touching downstream stages.

**Observability built into every stage**: OpenTelemetry traces, Prometheus metrics, and per-stage token accounting (input tokens, output tokens, est. cost, model, latency) on every request, indexed by correlation ID.
**Audit + recreatability** ("SR 26-2") — every assembled context window is logged with retrieved IDs, applied entitlements, model+prompt versions so any decision can be reconstructed.
**Docker Compose** stack with `dev` and `local-prod` profiles for one-command bring-up.

changes.name: stabilize-full-smoke
changes.why: The full smoke test no longer behaves like a smoke test: its default repository expands to thousands of chunks, each non-code chunk can trigger a paid cloud extraction call, and missing telemetry infrastructure adds repeated retry delays. The latest run processed only about 160 chunks in 18 minutes and projected hours of runtime, making the mandatory pre-push verification unreliable and financially unbounded.
what_changes: Add a committed, deterministic Git fixture that exercises text ingestion, Graphifyy code extraction, vector retrieval, candidate relationship review, traversal, and audit behavior with fewer than 20 chunks.
Make the default smoke independent of paid or external chat providers by adding an Ollama-compatible deterministic chat stub for structured graph-extraction responses.

Add an optional cloud canary mode that processes a strictly bounded number of chunks and verifies real provider credentials, structured output, and token accounting without becoming part of the default smoke.
Add hard overall and per-stage deadlines, child-process cleanup, stage timing, and actionable failure output to the smoke runner.
Add an OpenTelemetry Collector to the development stack and verify that ingestion and graph-extraction spans are accepted during the smoke. Offline runs may explicitly disable export.
Align the Qdrant client/server versions and fail readiness clearly when they are incompatible instead of emitting a warning throughout ingestion.
Make smoke assertions target only data created by the current run, so repeated executions do not tombstone or promote unrelated catalogue records.
Keep synchronous ingest-time extraction unchanged in this change. Decoupling extraction into a queue remains a separate architectural change.

changes.name: adopt-graphifyy
changes.why: We have built ~150 lines of file walking + chunking by hand. The git connector curates 35 file extensions and 9 skip-dirs in a Python set; the chunker splits on `\n\n` paragraph boundaries. For markdown and prose that's fine. For source code it is materially wrong: a 2000-character paragraph window splits mid-function and mid-class, and the resulting embeddings mix code from unrelated symbols.
what_changes: **Add `graphifyy>=0.8` as a dep on `services/ingestion`.** Base install pulls `networkx`, `numpy`, `rapidfuzz`, and ~28 tree-sitter language wheels (~50-100 MB). We do not opt into the `pdf`, `video`, `office`, `google`, `bedrock`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini` extras — those come in their own follow-up changes.

**Replace `walk_repo()` discovery body with `graphify.collect_files()`.** The git connector still clones, derives stable IDs, and computes content hashes — those are ours. The file-listing loop and the curated extension/skip-dir sets are deleted. `.graphifyignore` is honoured if present in the cloned repo.

**Type-aware chunking in `pipeline_runner.ingest_documents`.** Files whose extension is in the code set are chunked by graphifyy symbols (one chunk per function/class/method, with the text span fetched from the source). Files outside that set continue through the existing paragraph chunker.

**Deterministic code graph as a side effect of ingestion.** Each graphifyy symbol node lands as a `hive_mind.concept` row with `state = "confirmed"`, `confidence = 1.0`, `extractor_version = graphifyy/<version>`. Each graphifyy edge lands as a `hive_mind.relationship_edge` row with `state = "confirmed"`, `confidence` derived from the `EXTRACTED|INFERRED|AMBIGUOUS` label, `evidence_uri` pointing at the source chunk. Code edges skip the candidate review queue because tree-sitter output is deterministic — review provides no signal.
**Expand the relationship vocabulary** to include `calls`, `imports`, `uses` so graphifyy edges have first-class types. Seven seeded names becomes ten.

**Shrink the LLM extractor's scope to non-code** files (markdown, plain text, restructured text, html when we add it). The LLM path remains the candidate review path because language-model output is non-deterministic. Both paths feed the same Postgres+AGE tables; the admin UI does not differentiate.

**Per-stage token accounting** in `retrieval-pipeline` splits the `graph_extract` stage into `graph_extract_code` (deterministic, no tokens) and `graph_extract_text` (LLM, tokens). The Prometheus counters and OTel span attributes follow.

**Tests**: the existing chunker tests stay; new tests cover the symbol-chunker path with fixture Python and TypeScript files. The git connector test stays; new test wraps a tiny repo and asserts both text and code chunks are produced through the right path.

**Smoke**: extend the smoke to assert at least one node and one edge exist in `hive_mind.concept` / `hive_mind.relationship_edge` after the anthropic-cookbook re-ingest (it has Python notebooks + markdown).

changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

**New model client: `OllamaChat`.** A concrete chat client over the Ollama `/api/chat` shape with `Authorization: Bearer …` support (so it works against Ollama Cloud). The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Vocabulary CRUD.** Admin API to list, add, edit, and deprecate relationship types. The vocabulary table seeds with the seven defaults above; deployments can extend it. Inserts of edges with an unknown vocabulary `type` are rejected at the database level.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns the reachable subgraph as `{nodes, edges}` and includes only `confirmed` edges unless `include_candidates=true` is set.

**MCP `hive_mind/traverse_graph` tool wired up.** The tool's stub returning `not_implemented_in_mvp` is replaced with a real implementation that calls the pipeline's traverse endpoint and returns a structured payload.

**Admin UI graph page at `/graph`.** Three sub-views in one page: (1) a concept browser with filters (`state`, search by name), (2) a concept-detail view showing the concept's confirmed and candidate neighbours, and (3) a candidate review queue ordered by `confidence DESC` with per-row promote / edit / reject actions. **Tabular only — no visual graph rendering in this change.** A small status badge per concept indicates state.
**New shared types:** `Concept`, `ConceptListItem`, `RelationshipType`, `RelationshipEdge`, `EdgeState`, `TraverseRequest`, `TraverseResponse`, `ExtractionResult`.

changes.name: add-admin-vector-and-content
changes.why: The thin MVP gave operators a query review surface, but the user explicitly asked for an admin interface that also covers **vector search**, **review and management of content**, and **adding content**. Today the only way to see what's in the catalogue is to write SQL or curl Qdrant directly. That is fine for engineers, useless for operators, and makes the catalogue feel like a black box — which is the opposite of the architectural promise.
what_changes: New admin UI pages: - `/vectors` — vector search by free-text query, returning the top-K nearest catalog entities with score, source, classification, and a snippet. Drill-in shows the entity's nearest neighbours. - `/entities` — filterable, paginated entity browser (by source, classification, freshness). - `/entities/[id]` — entity detail: raw text, lineage (parent + chunks), source URI, metadata, freshness, recent audit appearances. Tombstone action. - `/ingestion` — configured connectors with last-run / next-run / error-count / status, plus a "Run now" panel that triggers a git ingest with a user-supplied URL.

New pipeline read endpoints (HTTP, JSON): - `GET /entities?source&classification&freshness_state&limit&offset` — list. - `GET /entities/{id}` — single entity with lineage children/parent. - `POST /search/vector` — `{query, top_k, filters?}` → ordered hits with `entity_id`, `score`, `payload`. Uses the same embeddings client the retrieval path uses; emits its own OTel span + token counter increment. - `DELETE /entities/{id}` — tombstone (sets `tombstoned_at`; cascades none). - `GET /ingestion/connectors` — connector list (proxies the ingestion service). - `POST /ingestion/git/run` — `{repo_url}` (proxies the ingestion service). - `GET /ingestion/runs/recent` — recent runs (proxies the ingestion service).

New ingestion HTTP surface (FastAPI, exposed inside the compose network only): - `POST /run/git` — kick off an ingest in a background task; return `{run_id, status:"queued"}`. - `GET /runs/recent` — in-memory list of recent runs (id, repo, started_at, finished_at, status, parents, chunks, error). - `GET /connectors` — `[{name: "git", supported: true}, ...]` mirroring the v0 capability set.
Shared types added to `packages/shared` and `packages/shared-py`: `Entity`, `EntityListItem`, `VectorSearchHit`, `IngestionRun`, `ConnectorStatus`.
New Storybook stories for every new component (`EntityRow`, `EntityDetail`, `VectorHit`, `ConnectorCard`, `IngestionRunRow`).
Vitest unit tests for every new admin UI component and the new pipeline endpoints (respx + httpx test client for the new routes; the existing patterns generalise).

pillars.title: Chunking
pillars.tagline: Cuts files into pieces small enough to search, without cutting mid-thought.
pillars.what:
The step that turns a whole file into a handful of searchable pieces. You cannot embed a 5,000-line file as a single vector and get useful results, because the meaning of everything averages out into mush.

openCG has two different choppers and picks between them based on file type. That split is the most interesting mechanic in the ingestion path.
pillars.why: Chunk boundaries decide search quality. A boundary in the wrong place gives you a result that starts mid-sentence and answers nothing. For prose, "the wrong place" means splitting an argument in half. For code, it means splitting a function in half, which is far worse, because half a function is not just less useful than the whole thing, it is actively misleading.

flow.title: Decide which chopper to use
flow.detail: is_code_path() asks whether the extension is one graphifyy can parse, then subtracts an explicit exclusion list. Prose formats like .md, .yaml, .json, and .html are forced down the text path even though graphifyy recognises them, because symbol-splitting a YAML file is meaningless.

flow.title: Prose path: pack paragraphs to a target size
flow.detail: Split the text on blank lines, then pack whole paragraphs into buckets of about 2,000 characters with a 200-character overlap between neighbours. The overlap means a sentence that straddles a boundary still appears complete in one of the two chunks. A single paragraph bigger than the target is hard-sliced with a stride of 1,800 characters.

flow.title: Code path: one chunk per symbol
flow.detail: Instead of splitting by size, parse the file into a syntax tree with graphifyy and emit one chunk per function, method, or class. A search hit then points at a whole coherent unit rather than an arbitrary window. Each chunk carries its symbol id, symbol kind, start and end lines, and parent scope as metadata.

flow.title: Fix up symbols that are too small or too large
flow.detail: Symbols under 50 characters get merged with adjacent symbols in the same parent scope, so a file of one-line getters does not become fifty near-useless chunks. Symbols over 8,000 characters get paragraph-split, and the resulting pieces are tagged split: true.

flow.title: Fall back safely
flow.detail: If graphifyy finds no symbols at all, or throws, the file quietly falls back to the prose chopper. A parser failure degrades chunk quality; it never drops the file.

flow.title: Mint deterministic chunk ids
flow.detail: Text chunks get uuid5(namespace, "{parent_id}:{chunk_index}"); symbol chunks get uuid5(namespace, "{parent_id}:{symbol_id}"). Fragment URIs read {source_uri}#chunk=3 or {source_uri}#symbol=<id>, so a result can always be traced back to a precise location.

gaps: graphifyy runs twice per code file — once for graph extraction and again inside the symbol chunker. Correct, but wasteful on large repositories.
No semantic chunking for prose. Boundaries are paragraph and character based; there is no model deciding where a topic actually ends.
Markdown structure is ignored. Headings do not influence boundaries, so a chunk can span two unrelated sections of a long document.

changes.name: add-incremental-ingest
changes.why: Every git re-ingest re-chunks and re-embeds the entire repository. `content_hash` is computed for every file, written to the catalog, and never read back — the only reads are for admin display. Embedding is one sequential HTTP call per chunk, so a repo producing 45,000 chunks pays 45,000 round trips on every run, plus a second model call per prose chunk for graph extraction. Fixing one typo costs the same as the first ingest.
what_changes: **A completion marker replaces the hash as the skip key.** Stored in the parent entity's existing `metadata` JSONB under a namespaced, versioned key, it records the `content_hash` that completed, an `embedding_fingerprint` (provider, model, vector dimension), a `chunker_version` (graphifyy version plus an application-controlled chunker format version and its constants), an `extraction_version`, the `chunk_mode` that was actually used, `chunk_count`, and `completed_at`.

**A file is skipped only when the marker parses, is a known version, and every identity component matches.** Absent, malformed, unknown-version, or any mismatch means process normally. Absent fails open by design: no existing row has a marker, so the first run after this ships reprocesses the corpus once.

**The marker is earned, not assumed.** It is written only after every chunk of that file embedded and upserted without error, extraction was not degraded, the code graph persisted where one was expected, and the file was not truncated mid-flight. Truncation is judged **per file**, not per run.

**The chunker reports why it produced text chunks.** `chunk_code_by_symbols` currently returns plain text chunks from two different places — extraction raised, or the file genuinely has no symbols — with identical return shape. The second is spec-mandated correct behaviour. Without distinguishing them, either degraded files freeze forever or every symbol-free source file reprocesses forever. The function gains an explicit outcome so the marker can tell them apart.

**Marker publication is compare-and-set.** Nothing serialises ingests — every `POST /run/git` spawns a background task — so two runs of the same repo can interleave. The write is conditional on the row still belonging to the attempt that did the work.
**Skipped files are still touched.** A skip bypasses `insert_entity`, so a lightweight catalog method refreshes verification state without rewriting content.

**Markers are invalidatable.** Recreating Qdrant collections is a documented operator procedure, after which every marker still passes and nothing re-ingests. An explicit invalidation path prevents that trap.

**Runs report what they skipped.** `IngestionSummary`, `RunStore`, `GET /runs/recent`, and the admin ingestion page all carry a skipped count. This is a safety surface, not cosmetics: an over-aggressive gate is otherwise invisible.

changes.name: adopt-graphifyy
changes.why: We have built ~150 lines of file walking + chunking by hand. The git connector curates 35 file extensions and 9 skip-dirs in a Python set; the chunker splits on `\n\n` paragraph boundaries. For markdown and prose that's fine. what_changes: **Add `graphifyy>=0.8` as a dep on `services/ingestion`.** Base install pulls `networkx`, `numpy`, `rapidfuzz`, and ~28 tree-sitter language wheels (~50-100 MB). We do not opt into the `pdf`, `video`, `office`, `google`, `bedrock`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini` extras — those come in their own follow-up changes.

**Replace `walk_repo()` discovery body with `graphify.collect_files()`.** The git connector still clones, derives stable IDs, and computes content hashes — those are ours. The file-listing loop and the curated extension/skip-dir sets are deleted. `.graphifyignore` is honoured if present in the cloned repo.

changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). pillars.title: Model Providers
pillars.tagline: Two model clients: local embeddings, and cloud chat for extraction.
pillars.what:
The layer that talks to AI models. There are exactly two clients, deliberately kept concrete rather than hidden behind an abstraction:

OllamaEmbeddings turns text into vectors, running locally. OllamaChat asks a chat model for structured JSON, used only by the knowledge-graph extractor.
pillars.why:
Every model call costs money, leaks data, or both, so they are funnelled through two auditable places rather than scattered across the codebase. Every call also reports its token usage, which is what makes per-stage cost accounting possible.

The split between local and cloud is not a design preference — it is a constraint that was discovered by probing. The Ollama Cloud key available to this project returns 200 on /api/tags and /api/chat but 401 on /api/embed for every model tried. So embeddings must run locally, and the cloud key is chat-only.

flow.title: Embeddings: pick the working API path
flow.detail: OllamaEmbeddings first tries POST /api/embed with {"model", "input"}. On a 404 it falls back to the older POST /api/embeddings with {"model", "prompt"}, then remembers which one worked for the rest of the client's life so it does not re-probe on every call.

flow.title: Embeddings: return the vector and a token estimate
flow.detail: The default model nomic-embed-text returns 768 floats. Tokens are estimated rather than measured, at roughly one token per four characters, since the embeddings endpoint does not report usage.

flow.title: Chat: request JSON, not prose
flow.detail: OllamaChat calls POST /api/chat with format: "json" and a Bearer token, so it works against Ollama Cloud. It is given a system prompt and a response schema and returns content plus real token counts.

flow.title: Report tokens on every call
flow.detail: Each call increments opencg_tokens_total{stage,model,provider,tenant,direction} and sets matching OpenTelemetry span attributes. This is treated as non-negotiable in the project rules: a model call that does not report tokens is a bug.

flow.title: Degrade instead of failing
flow.detail: An embedding failure logs and skips that one chunk rather than aborting the run. An extraction failure is caught, counted, and stepped over. Model calls are treated as unreliable by default.

facts: The Ollama Cloud key is chat-only — /api/embed returns 401 for this account
gaps: No provider abstraction. Two concrete clients, no EmbeddingProvider / Reranker / Generator protocols. The add-foundation spec describes them; they are deliberately deferred until a third caller exists so the abstraction is not invented from one example.
No embedding cache. Identical text embedded twice costs twice, even in the same run.
No retry or backoff. A transient provider blip drops a chunk silently rather than retrying it.
No Anthropic or OpenAI adapter, despite being named in the full vision.

changes.name: add-ontology-layer
changes.why: The knowledge graph shipped with typed *edges* and untyped *nodes*. `relationship_vocab` constrains the ten legal arrow names, but a `concept` row is just a name, a description, and an aliases array. Nothing records that `parse_config` is a **function**, that `Prompt Caching` is a **topic**, or that `checks.py` is a **module** — and nothing prevents the extractor from emitting `"Prompt Caching" calls "Anthropic API"`, which is meaningless.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: the ontology class.** A named kind of thing (`Function`, `Module`, `Service`, `Topic`, `Document`) with a stable `class_id`, a canonical `name`, a `description`, an optional `parent_class_id`, and a `state` reflecting whether it is part of the seeded core or operator-authored.

**A single-parent subtype hierarchy.** Classes form a tree rooted at `Thing`. Subsumption is transitive: if `Method` is a subtype of `Function` and `Function` is a subtype of `CodeSymbol`, then a `Method` satisfies any constraint written against `CodeSymbol`. Cycles are rejected; a class may not be its own ancestor.

**Concepts gain a class.** `opencg.concept` gains a nullable `class_id` FK. Nullable, not `NOT NULL`, because every concept extracted before this change is genuinely unclassified and pretending otherwise would be a lie in the data. Unclassified concepts sort to the top of the review queue.

**Domain/range constraints on relationship types.** A new table declares which `(domain class, relationship type, range class)` triples are legal — `calls` runs `Function → Function`, `defined_in` runs `CodeSymbol → Module`, `depends_on` runs `Service → Service`. A relationship type with no constraint rows is unconstrained, so existing behaviour is preserved until an operator narrows it.

**The relationship vocabulary is absorbed into the ontology.** `opencg.relationship_vocab` becomes `opencg.ontology_relationship`, and edge types are governed by the ontology's admin API, audit vocabulary, and version rather than by a surface of their own. `name` stays the primary key, so `relationship_edge.type`'s foreign key — and the guarantee that an unknown edge type fails at the database — survives the rename untouched. `/graph/vocab` stays as a deprecated alias for one release. Classes, relationship types, and constraints are one model, versioned together.

**A seeded core ontology, extensible per deployment.** Ships with a small tree covering what openCG actually ingests today — code symbols and documents — plus the constraints for the six code relations graphifyy emits. Operators add classes and constraints through the admin API; nothing about the core is privileged at query time.

**Type-aware extraction.** The prose extractor's prompt is rebuilt from the ontology rather than hardcoded: it names the legal classes, asks the model to classify each concept it emits, and names the legal `(domain, relation, range)` triples instead of a bare list of relation names. The code path classifies deterministically from graphifyy's `symbol_kind`, which already distinguishes `class` / `function` / `method` / `module`.

**Constraint checking is advisory, never fatal.** An edge that violates a constraint is still written, marked `constraint_violation`, and routed to review. It is excluded from traversal by default exactly as a candidate is. Hard database rejection was rejected as an option: it would make a schema edit retroactively destroy extracted data, and it would give ingestion a new way to fail.
**Class-filtered traversal.** `GET /graph/traverse` accepts a `classes` parameter, filtering returned nodes by class with subtype expansion.
**Admin UI `/ontology` page.** A class-tree editor, a constraint matrix per relationship type, and a violations queue. Every ontology edit writes to the existing append-only `graph_audit_log`.

pillars.title: Vector Index
pillars.tagline: Qdrant. Finds text that means the same thing, not just text that matches.
pillars.what: A Qdrant database that does exactly one job well: given 768 numbers, find the closest stored points. That is what makes semantic search work — asking about "login flow" can surface a chunk about "authentication handshake" even though the two share no words.
pillars.why:
Keyword search fails whenever the asker and the author chose different vocabulary, which in a large organisation is most of the time. Vector search fixes that by comparing meaning instead of spelling.

Qdrant is treated as a disposable index, not a database of record. Every vector can be rebuilt from Postgres, which means it can be wiped and re-created without data loss.

flow.title: Write a point per chunk
flow.detail: Each chunk becomes one Qdrant point. The point id is the chunk's UUID from the catalog, so Postgres and Qdrant always agree on identity and re-ingesting overwrites cleanly instead of duplicating.

flow.title: Store a payload alongside the vector
flow.detail: A small denormalised copy travels with the vector: tenant, entity_id, parent_entity_id, source, source_uri, title, the raw text, classification, chunk_index, and symbol_id for code. This lets a search return readable results without a round trip to Postgres.

flow.title: Route into a per-source collection
flow.detail: Collections are named {collection_prefix}{source}, so git content lands in default__git. Splitting by source means one connector can be re-indexed without touching the others.

flow.title: Search at query time
flow.detail: search() embeds the query, asks every matching collection for its top k, then sorts the merged list by raw score. The admin explorer uses search_all() instead, which fuses across collections with reciprocal rank fusion so no single collection dominates on score scale alone.

pillars.tagline: One Postgres table holding the authoritative copy of everything.
pillars.what:
The single Postgres table opencg.entity that holds the real copy of every document and every chunk. Full text, metadata, provenance, lineage.

The mental model that matters: Postgres is the truth, Qdrant is an index. If they ever disagree, Postgres wins and the index gets rebuilt.

flow.title: Write a parent row per file
flow.detail: Every ingested file gets one row: title, full body, content hash, git revision, source URI, classification, and a JSONB metadata blob.

flow.title: Write a child row per chunk
flow.detail: Each chunk gets its own row with parent_entity_id pointing at the file. That parent-child link is the lineage the admin UI walks when it shows you where a search result came from.

flow.title: Upsert rather than insert
flow.detail: Writes are ON CONFLICT (tenant, source, source_uri) DO UPDATE, refreshing body, title, hash, metadata, and revision, clearing any tombstone, and resetting freshness_state to fresh. Re-ingestion updates in place instead of duplicating.

flow.title: Index for keyword search
flow.detail: Two GIN indexes make this table a search engine in its own right: a full-text index over title || body, and a trigram index for fuzzy and partial matching. Together they power the lexical half of retrieval.

flow.title: Serve the lexical leg
flow.detail: lexical_search() runs full-text plus trigram matching, scoped to tenant = $1 and excluding tombstoned rows, and returns ranked hits with their full text ready to assemble.

flow.title: Delete softly
flow.detail: Removing an entity sets tombstoned_at rather than deleting the row, so audit records that reference it stay meaningful forever.

Indexes: FTS on title || body, trigram GIN on body and title

No revision history. An upsert overwrites the previous body, so you cannot see what a document used to say — only what it says now.

changes.name: add-incremental-ingest
changes.why: Every git re-ingest re-chunks and re-embeds the entire repository. `content_hash` is computed for every file, written to the catalog, and never read back — the only reads are for admin display. Embedding is one sequential HTTP call per chunk, so a repo producing 45,000 chunks pays 45,000 round trips on every run, plus a second model call per prose chunk for graph extraction. Fixing one typo costs the same as the first ingest.
what_changes: **A completion marker replaces the hash as the skip key.** Stored in the parent entity's existing `metadata` JSONB under a namespaced, versioned key, it records the `content_hash` that completed, an `embedding_fingerprint` (provider, model, vector dimension), a `chunker_version` (graphifyy version plus an application-controlled chunker format version and its constants), an `extraction_version`, the `chunk_mode` that was actually used, `chunk_count`, and `completed_at`.

**A file is skipped only when the marker parses, is a known version, and every identity component matches.** Absent, malformed, unknown-version, or any mismatch means process normally. Absent fails open by design: no existing row has a marker, so the first run after this ships reprocesses the corpus once.

**The marker is earned, not assumed.** It is written only after every chunk of that file embedded and upserted without error, extraction was not degraded, the code graph persisted where one was expected, and the file was not truncated mid-flight. Truncation is judged **per file**, not per run.

**The chunker reports why it produced text chunks.** `chunk_code_by_symbols` currently returns plain text chunks from two different places — extraction raised, or the file genuinely has no symbols — with identical return shape. The second is spec-mandated correct behaviour. Without distinguishing them, either degraded files freeze forever or every symbol-free source file reprocesses forever. The function gains an explicit outcome so the marker can tell them apart.

**Marker publication is compare-and-set.** Nothing serialises ingests — every `POST /run/git` spawns a background task — so two runs of the same repo can interleave. The write is conditional on the row still belonging to the attempt that did the work.
**Skipped files are still touched.** A skip bypasses `insert_entity`, so a lightweight catalog method refreshes verification state without rewriting content.

**Markers are invalidatable.** Recreating Qdrant collections is a documented operator procedure, after which every marker still passes and nothing re-ingests. An explicit invalidation path prevents that trap.

**Runs report what they skipped.** `IngestionSummary`, `RunStore`, `GET /runs/recent`, and the admin ingestion page all carry a skipped count. This is a safety surface, not cosmetics: an over-aggressive gate is otherwise invisible.

pillars.title: Knowledge Graph
pillars.tagline: Concepts and named relationships between them, extracted automatically and reviewed by a human.
pillars.what:
The part that goes beyond "documents matching your words". Instead of storing documents, it stores ideas and named connections between ideas.

"Prompt Caching" depends_on "Anthropic API". Function parse_config calls function load_yaml. Module server imports module router.

Four tables do the work: concept holds the nodes, relationship_edge holds typed arrows, relationship_evidence records which source chunk justified each arrow, and relationship_vocab constrains which arrow types are even legal.
pillars.why:
Search answers "what mentions this". A graph answers "what is connected to this, and how" — which is the question people actually ask when they are trying to understand a system rather than look up a fact.

The design's central safety idea is the candidate / confirmed split. Code parsing is deterministic and lands as confirmed. An LLM's guesses land as candidate and stay quarantined out of traversal results until a human promotes them. That is what makes automatic extraction safe to run at all.

flow.title: Constrain the vocabulary first
flow.detail: Only ten relationship names are legal, seeded at database init: depends_on, defined_in, supersedes, mentions, related_to, causes, derived_from, calls, imports, uses. A foreign key on the edge table means an unknown type is rejected by the database, not just by application code.

flow.title: Code path: parse, do not guess
flow.detail: For source files, graphifyy walks the syntax tree and reads off exactly which function calls which and which module imports what. No model, no tokens, no hallucination. These edges land as state = 'confirmed' with confidence = 1.0, because parsing is not an opinion.

flow.title: Prose path: ask a model for JSON
flow.detail: For text chunks, the chunk is sent to gemma3:4b with a prompt that names the ten legal relations and asks for {concepts, relations} JSON with a confidence per relation. Concept names are requested as short noun phrases; the model is told to be conservative and emit only what the text clearly supports. Input is truncated at 8,000 characters.

flow.title: Distrust the model's output
flow.detail: The response is parsed defensively — code fences stripped, the first {...} span extracted, schema-validated. Then anything using a relation outside the vocabulary is dropped, and anything below 0.6 confidence is dropped. What survives is written as state = 'candidate'.

flow.title: Never fail the ingest
flow.detail: Extraction is best-effort by rule. A timeout, a parse failure, or an unavailable model increments opencg_extractor_errors_total{reason}, logs a warning naming the chunk, and lets ingestion continue. One bad chunk cannot break a run.

flow.title: Deduplicate concepts on a normalised key

changes.name: add-ontology-layer
changes.why: The knowledge graph shipped with typed *edges* and untyped *nodes*. `relationship_vocab` constrains the ten legal arrow names, but a `concept` row is just a name, a description, and an aliases array. Nothing records that `parse_config` is a **function**, that `Prompt Caching` is a **topic**, or that `checks.py` is a **module** — and nothing prevents the extractor from emitting `"Prompt Caching" calls "Anthropic API"`, which is meaningless.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: the ontology class.** A named kind of thing (`Function`, `Module`, `Service`, `Topic`, `Document`) with a stable `class_id`, a canonical `name`, a `description`, an optional `parent_class_id`, and a `state` reflecting whether it is part of the seeded core or operator-authored.

**A single-parent subtype hierarchy.** Classes form a tree rooted at `Thing`. Subsumption is transitive: if `Method` is a subtype of `Function` and `Function` is a subtype of `CodeSymbol`, then a `Method` satisfies any constraint written against `CodeSymbol`. Cycles are rejected; a class may not be its own ancestor.

**Concepts gain a class.** `opencg.concept` gains a nullable `class_id` FK. Nullable, not `NOT NULL`, because every concept extracted before this change is genuinely unclassified and pretending otherwise would be a lie in the data. Unclassified concepts sort to the top of the review queue.

**Domain/range constraints on relationship types.** A new table declares which `(domain class, relationship type, range class)` triples are legal — `calls` runs `Function → Function`, `defined_in` runs `CodeSymbol → Module`, `depends_on` runs `Service → Service`. A relationship type with no constraint rows is unconstrained, so existing behaviour is preserved until an operator narrows it.

**The relationship vocabulary is absorbed into the ontology.** `opencg.relationship_vocab` becomes `opencg.ontology_relationship`, and edge types are governed by the ontology's admin API, audit vocabulary, and version rather than by a surface of their own. `name` stays the primary key, so `relationship_edge.type`'s foreign key — and the guarantee that an unknown edge type fails at the database — survives the rename untouched. `/graph/vocab` stays as a deprecated alias for one release. Classes, relationship types, and constraints are one model, versioned together.

**A seeded core ontology, extensible per deployment.** Ships with a small tree covering what openCG actually ingests today — code symbols and documents — plus the constraints for the six code relations graphifyy emits. Operators add classes and constraints through the admin API; nothing about the core is privileged at query time.

**Type-aware extraction.** The prose extractor's prompt is rebuilt from the ontology rather than hardcoded: it names the legal classes, asks the model to classify each concept it emits, and names the legal `(domain, relation, range)` triples instead of a bare list of relation names. **Constraint checking is advisory, never fatal.** An edge that violates a constraint is still written, marked `constraint_violation`, and routed to review. It is excluded from traversal by default exactly as a candidate is. Hard database rejection was rejected as an option: it would make a schema edit retroactively destroy extracted data, and it would give ingestion a new way to fail.
**Class-filtered traversal.** `GET /graph/traverse` accepts a `classes` parameter, filtering returned nodes by class with subtype expansion.

changes.name: add-incremental-ingest
changes.why: Every git re-ingest re-chunks and re-embeds the entire repository. `content_hash` is computed for every file, written to the catalog, and never read back — the only reads are for admin display. Embedding is one sequential HTTP call per chunk, so a repo producing 45,000 chunks pays 45,000 round trips on every run, plus a second model call per prose chunk for graph extraction. Fixing one typo costs the same as the first ingest.
what_changes: **A completion marker replaces the hash as the skip key.** Stored in the parent entity's existing `metadata` JSONB under a namespaced, versioned key, it records the `content_hash` that completed, an `embedding_fingerprint` (provider, model, vector dimension), a `chunker_version` (graphifyy version plus an application-controlled chunker format version and its constants), an `extraction_version`, the `chunk_mode` that was actually used, `chunk_count`, and `completed_at`.

**A file is skipped only when the marker parses, is a known version, and every identity component matches.** Absent, malformed, unknown-version, or any mismatch means process normally. Absent fails open by design: no existing row has a marker, so the first run after this ships reprocesses the corpus once.

**The marker is earned, not assumed.** It is written only after every chunk of that file embedded and upserted without error, extraction was not degraded, the code graph persisted where one was expected, and the file was not truncated mid-flight. Truncation is judged **per file**, not per run.

**The chunker reports why it produced text chunks.** `chunk_code_by_symbols` currently returns plain text chunks from two different places — extraction raised, or the file genuinely has no symbols — with identical return shape. The second is spec-mandated correct behaviour. Without distinguishing them, either degraded files freeze forever or every symbol-free source file reprocesses forever. The function gains an explicit outcome so the marker can tell them apart.

**Marker publication is compare-and-set.** Nothing serialises ingests — every `POST /run/git` spawns a background task — so two runs of the same repo can interleave. The write is conditional on the row still belonging to the attempt that did the work.
**Skipped files are still touched.** A skip bypasses `insert_entity`, so a lightweight catalog method refreshes verification state without rewriting content.

**Markers are invalidatable.** Recreating Qdrant collections is a documented operator procedure, after which every marker still passes and nothing re-ingests. An explicit invalidation path prevents that trap.

**Runs report what they skipped.** `IngestionSummary`, `RunStore`, `GET /runs/recent`, and the admin ingestion page all carry a skipped count. This is a safety surface, not cosmetics: an over-aggressive gate is otherwise invisible.

changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

**New model client: `OllamaChat`.** A concrete chat client over the Ollama `/api/chat` shape with `Authorization: Bearer …` support (so it works against Ollama Cloud). The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Vocabulary CRUD.** Admin API to list, add, edit, and deprecate relationship types. The vocabulary table seeds with the seven defaults above; deployments can extend it. Inserts of edges with an unknown vocabulary `type` are rejected at the database level.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns the reachable subgraph as `{nodes, edges}` and includes only `confirmed` edges unless `include_candidates=true` is set.

**MCP `hive_mind/traverse_graph` tool wired up.** The tool's stub returning `not_implemented_in_mvp` is replaced with a real implementation that calls the pipeline's traverse endpoint and returns a structured payload.

**New shared types:** `Concept`, `ConceptListItem`, `RelationshipType`, `RelationshipEdge`, `EdgeState`, `TraverseRequest`, `TraverseResponse`, `ExtractionResult`.

pillars.title: Ontology
pillars.tagline: The schema the graph does not have yet — what kinds of things exist, and which relationships are legal between which kinds.
pillars.what:
Nothing yet. This pillar is specified, not built. Every step below describes what add-ontology-layer says will happen, and each one links to the spec that says it rather than to code, because there is no code.

The knowledge graph shipped with typed edges and untyped nodes. relationship_vocab makes type = "nonsense" fail at the database, but a concept row is only a name, a description, and an aliases array. Nothing records that parse_config is a *function*, that Prompt Caching is a *topic*, or that checks.py is a *module*.

The ontology is the missing half: a tree of classes saying what kinds of things exist, and domain/range constraints saying which relationship types may run between which kinds — calls connects a Function to a Function, defined_in connects a code symbol to a module.

It also takes custody of the arrow names. The relationship vocabulary moves out of the graph and into the ontology as ontology_relationship, so classes, relationship types, and constraints are one model with one admin API, one audit vocabulary, and one version.
pillars.why:
Without it, "Prompt Caching" calls "Anthropic API" is an edge the system has no way to recognise as nonsense. The extractor is handed ten relation names and nothing about what may sit on either end, so the only filter on a bad guess is a confidence score the model reports about itself.

Three things get sharper the moment kinds exist. Extraction gets a bounded space to guess in. Review gets leverage, because "reject every calls edge whose source is not a code symbol" becomes one rule instead of a hundred clicks. And traversal gets a type filter, so "the services this depends on, not the docs that mention it" becomes answerable.

flow.title: Kinds form a tree
flow.detail: Thing at the root; CodeSymbol, Document, Service, and Topic beneath it; Module, Class, Function, and ExternalPackage beneath CodeSymbol; and Method beneath Function. Single parent only — no multiple inheritance — because subsumption over a tree is a recursive walk anyone can read, and a DAG would need diamond-resolution rules that nothing in the corpus asks for.

flow.title: The arrow names move in too
flow.detail: relationship_vocab is renamed ontology_relationship and governed by the ontology rather than by the graph. name stays the primary key, so the foreign key that makes an unknown edge type a database error survives the rename untouched and no edge row is rewritten. A half-schema that says what kinds of things exist but not what kinds of arrows exist would have left an operator editing one model through two APIs.

flow.title: Constraints narrow, they never widen
flow.detail: A constraint declares one legal (domain, relation, range) triple. A relationship type with no constraints accepts anything, so the day the layer lands nothing existing becomes illegal. The seed constrains only the five relations the code extractor emits and leaves mentions, related_to, supersedes, causes, and derived_from deliberately open.

flow.title: Subtypes inherit their ancestors' constraints
flow.detail: calls is written once as Function → Function. A Method satisfies it because Method sits under Function. Ancestry is resolved with a recursive SQL walk rather than a cached closure table, because the tree holds tens of rows and a cache that must be invalidated on every edit is a correctness liability bought for speed nobody needs.

flow.title: The code path classifies for free
flow.detail: graphifyy already distinguishes class, function, method, and module — it writes that into chunk metadata as symbol_kind and the graph writer currently throws it away. Mapping it onto ontology classes costs no model call and no tokens, and gives the graph a correctly-typed backbone to measure everything else against.

flow.title: The prose path gets a generated prompt
flow.detail: extract.py's hardcoded relation list is replaced by a prompt rendered from the live ontology: the class names, and the legal triples instead of bare relation names. The model is asked to classify each concept it emits. An operator adding a class changes the next chunk's prompt with no deploy and no code change.

flow.title: Violations are recorded, never rejected
flow.detail: An edge that breaks a constraint is still written, marked violation, and hidden from traversal the same way a candidate is. Hard rejection was considered and refused twice over: it would give ingestion a new way to fail a chunk, and it would turn an admin's schema edit into a destructive data operation against rows extracted under the old schema.

flow.title: Unclassified is a real answer
flow.detail: concept.class_id is nullable, and an edge with an unclassified endpoint stays unchecked rather than becoming a violation. Every concept extracted before the ontology existed is genuinely of unknown kind; defaulting it to the root class would store a lie that no query could tell apart from a deliberate choice.

flow.title: Editing the schema re-checks, it does not rewrite
flow.detail: Adding or removing a constraint marks the affected edges unchecked and re-evaluates them. It never touches an edge's state. The two axes stay independent on purpose: state is what a human decided, constraint_state is what the schema says.

flow.title: Review in the admin UI
flow.detail: A planned /ontology page holds three surfaces: the class tree, a constraint matrix per relationship type, and a violations queue. The queue offers "reclassify endpoint" alongside promote and reject, because a violation is as often a mis-typed node as a wrong edge.

pillars.title: Retrieval Pipeline
pillars.tagline: Turns a question into a token-budgeted packet of relevant context.
pillars.what:
The FastAPI service that answers the central question: given a query, which pieces of the corpus should an AI model see, and in what order, within a fixed token budget?

It runs two searches at once, merges them, applies policy, trims to budget, and logs everything it did.
pillars.why: An AI model with a 200k context window still gives worse answers when you fill it with marginally relevant text. The scarce resource is not storage, it is attention. This pillar exists to spend a token budget well and to be able to prove afterwards how it was spent.

flow.title: Check identity
flow.detail: Confirms principal and tenant are present on the request envelope and passes them through. There is no authentication here — identity arrives pre-declared by the caller.

flow.title: Run dense and lexical search in parallel
flow.detail: The dense leg embeds the question with the same nomic-embed-text model used at ingest and asks Qdrant for the nearest chunks. The lexical leg runs Postgres full-text and trigram search for literal matches. Both run under one asyncio.gather, so the slower one sets the latency.

flow.title: Fuse the two rankings
flow.detail: The legs are merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion: each result scores 1 / (60 + rank) from each list, and the scores add. Something ranking well in both lists floats to the top. The constant 60 damps the head so no single list dominates. There is no model and no tuning here — it works on ranks, not scores, which is why it survives the two legs having incomparable score scales.

flow.title: Merge metadata from both legs
flow.detail: Each candidate is annotated with which legs found it. If Qdrant's payload was missing text, the Postgres copy fills it in — the catalog is always the fallback for truth.

flow.title: Apply the classification policy
flow.detail: Each candidate's classification is checked against the caller's roles. A role that is not recognised gets public only. Denials are recorded as classification_restricted rather than silently dropped.

flow.title: Fill the token budget top-down
flow.detail: Walk candidates in fused-score order, estimating tokens at 0.25 per character, and stop including once the budget is reached. Everything that does not fit is recorded as budget_exhausted. Default budget: 4,000 tokens.

flow.title: Hash the result and audit it
flow.detail: The surviving fragments are hashed with SHA-256 over ordered (entity_id, score, text) to produce final_context_hash, then one audit row is written capturing every candidate and its verdict. The response returns fragments, usage, and the hash.

facts: Response includes a SHA-256 final_context_hash over the exact assembled context
gaps: filters on /retrieve is a no-op. The field exists on the request type and is accepted, but never reaches the retrieval stage. Filtering only works on the admin vector-search route.
No reranker and no score threshold. Fusion, policy, and budget are the only ranking forces; a cross-encoder rerank stage is specced but deferred.
No intent classification. The full design has a stage that routes a query by intent; the shipped path skips straight from identity to hybrid retrieval.
Entitlement is a hardcoded dict, not real policy. OPA-backed enforcement is deferred.
No route authentication. The service assumes a trusted internal Docker network.
The knowledge graph is not consulted here. Graph-aware retrieval is a planned follow-up.

changes.name: add-ontology-layer
changes.why: The knowledge graph shipped with typed *edges* and untyped *nodes*. `relationship_vocab` constrains the ten legal arrow names, but a `concept` row is just a name, a description, and an aliases array. Nothing records that `parse_config` is a **function**, that `Prompt Caching` is a **topic**, or that `checks.py` is a **module** — and nothing prevents the extractor from emitting `"Prompt Caching" calls "Anthropic API"`, which is meaningless.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: the ontology class.** A named kind of thing (`Function`, `Module`, `Service`, `Topic`, `Document`) with a stable `class_id`, a canonical `name`, a `description`, an optional `parent_class_id`, and a `state` reflecting whether it is part of the seeded core or operator-authored.

**A single-parent subtype hierarchy.** Classes form a tree rooted at `Thing`. Subsumption is transitive: if `Method` is a subtype of `Function` and `Function` is a subtype of `CodeSymbol`, then a `Method` satisfies any constraint written against `CodeSymbol`. Cycles are rejected; a class may not be its own ancestor.

**Concepts gain a class.** `opencg.concept` gains a nullable `class_id` FK. Nullable, not `NOT NULL`, because every concept extracted before this change is genuinely unclassified and pretending otherwise would be a lie in the data. Unclassified concepts sort to the top of the review queue.

**Domain/range constraints on relationship types.** A new table declares which `(domain class, relationship type, range class)` triples are legal — `calls` runs `Function → Function`, `defined_in` runs `CodeSymbol → Module`, `depends_on` runs `Service → Service`. A relationship type with no constraint rows is unconstrained, so existing behaviour is preserved until an operator narrows it.

**The relationship vocabulary is absorbed into the ontology.** `opencg.relationship_vocab` becomes `opencg.ontology_relationship`, and edge types are governed by the ontology's admin API, audit vocabulary, and version rather than by a surface of their own. `name` stays the primary key, so `relationship_edge.type`'s foreign key — and the guarantee that an unknown edge type fails at the database — survives the rename untouched. `/graph/vocab` stays as a deprecated alias for one release. Classes, relationship types, and constraints are one model, versioned together.

**A seeded core ontology, extensible per deployment.** Ships with a small tree covering what openCG actually ingests today — code symbols and documents — plus the constraints for the six code relations graphifyy emits. Operators add classes and constraints through the admin API; nothing about the core is privileged at query time.

**Type-aware extraction.** The prose extractor's prompt is rebuilt from the ontology rather than hardcoded: it names the legal classes, asks the model to classify each concept it emits, and names the legal `(domain, relation, range)` triples instead of a bare list of relation names. The code path classifies deterministically from graphifyy's `symbol_kind`, which already distinguishes `class` / `function` / `method` / `module`.

**Constraint checking is advisory, never fatal.** An edge that violates a constraint is still written, marked `constraint_violation`, and routed to review. It is excluded from traversal by default exactly as a candidate is. Hard database rejection was rejected as an option: it would make a schema edit retroactively destroy extracted data, and it would give ingestion a new way to fail.
**Class-filtered traversal.** `GET /graph/traverse` accepts a `classes` parameter, filtering returned nodes by class with subtype expansion.
**Admin UI `/ontology` page.** A class-tree editor, a constraint matrix per relationship type, and a violations queue. Every ontology edit writes to the existing append-only `graph_audit_log`.

changes.name: adopt-graphifyy
changes.why: We have built ~150 lines of file walking + chunking by hand. The git connector curates 35 file extensions and 9 skip-dirs in a Python set; the chunker splits on `\n\n` paragraph boundaries. For markdown and prose that's fine. For source code it is materially wrong: a 2000-character paragraph window splits mid-function and mid-class, and the resulting embeddings mix code from unrelated symbols.
what_changes: **Add `graphifyy>=0.8` as a dep on `services/ingestion`.** Base install pulls `networkx`, `numpy`, `rapidfuzz`, and ~28 tree-sitter language wheels (~50-100 MB). We do not opt into the `pdf`, `video`, `office`, `google`, `bedrock`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini` extras — those come in their own follow-up changes.

**Replace `walk_repo()` discovery body with `graphify.collect_files()`.** The git connector still clones, derives stable IDs, and computes content hashes — those are ours. The file-listing loop and the curated extension/skip-dir sets are deleted. `.graphifyignore` is honoured if present in the cloned repo.

**Type-aware chunking in `pipeline_runner.ingest_documents`.** Files whose extension is in the code set are chunked by graphifyy symbols (one chunk per function/class/method, with the text span fetched from the source). Files outside that set continue through the existing paragraph chunker.

**Deterministic code graph as a side effect of ingestion.** Each graphifyy symbol node lands as a `hive_mind.concept` row with `state = "confirmed"`, `confidence = 1.0`, `extractor_version = graphifyy/<version>`. Each graphifyy edge lands as a `hive_mind.relationship_edge` row with `state = "confirmed"`, `confidence` derived from the `EXTRACTED|INFERRED|AMBIGUOUS` label, `evidence_uri` pointing at the source chunk. Code edges skip the candidate review queue because tree-sitter output is deterministic — review provides no signal.
**Expand the relationship vocabulary** to include `calls`, `imports`, `uses` so graphifyy edges have first-class types. Seven seeded names becomes ten.

**Shrink the LLM extractor's scope to non-code** files (markdown, plain text, restructured text, html when we add it). The LLM path remains the candidate review path because language-model output is non-deterministic. Both paths feed the same Postgres+AGE tables; the admin UI does not differentiate.

**Per-stage token accounting** in `retrieval-pipeline` splits the `graph_extract` stage into `graph_extract_code` (deterministic, no tokens) and `graph_extract_text` (LLM, tokens). The Prometheus counters and OTel span attributes follow.

**Tests**: the existing chunker tests stay; new tests cover the symbol-chunker path with fixture Python and TypeScript files. The git connector test stays; new test wraps a tiny repo and asserts both text and code chunks are produced through the right path.

**Smoke**: extend the smoke to assert at least one node and one edge exist in `hive_mind.concept` / `hive_mind.relationship_edge` after the anthropic-cookbook re-ingest (it has Python notebooks + markdown).
