changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

**New model client: `OllamaChat`.** A concrete chat client over the Ollama `/api/chat` shape with `Authorization: Bearer …` support (so it works against Ollama Cloud). The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Vocabulary CRUD.** Admin API to list, add, edit, and deprecate relationship types. The vocabulary table seeds with the seven defaults above; deployments can extend it. Inserts of edges with an unknown vocabulary `type` are rejected at the database level.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns the reachable subgraph as `{nodes, edges}` and includes only `confirmed` edges unless `include_candidates=true` is set.

**MCP `hive_mind/traverse_graph` tool wired up.** The tool's stub returning `not_implemented_in_mvp` is replaced with a real implementation that calls the pipeline's traverse endpoint and returns a structured payload.

**Admin UI graph page at `/graph`.** Three sub-views in one page: (1) a concept browser with filters (`state`, search by name), (2) a concept-detail view showing the concept's confirmed and candidate neighbours, and (3) a candidate review queue ordered by `confidence DESC` with per-row promote / edit / reject actions. **Tabular only — no visual graph rendering in this change.** A small status badge per concept indicates state.
**New shared types:** `Concept`, `ConceptListItem`, `RelationshipType`, `RelationshipEdge`, `EdgeState`, `TraverseRequest`, `TraverseResponse`, `ExtractionResult`.

pillars.title: MCP Server
pillars.tagline: The standard plug that lets Cursor or Claude call into openCG.
pillars.what:
A small TypeScript service that speaks Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets AI tools discover and call external capabilities. It is the reason openCG is useful from inside an editor rather than only from a browser.

It is a thin adapter by design: it validates arguments, forwards to the pipeline over HTTP, and formats the reply. No retrieval logic lives here.
pillars.why: Without MCP, every AI tool would need a bespoke integration. With it, one server makes the whole knowledge catalogue available to Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and anything else that speaks the protocol.

flow.title: Advertise the tool list
flow.detail: Five tools are declared with JSON schemas. Two are real: opencg/retrieve_for_context and opencg/traverse_graph. Three (search, get_entity, submit_feedback) are advertised but return not_implemented_in_mvp, so clients can see the intended surface.

flow.title: Accept a call over stdio or HTTP
flow.detail: Both transports run in the same process. stdio serves clients that launch the server as a subprocess, typically docker run -i. Streamable HTTP serves clients that connect by URL at ALL /mcp, with stateful sessions keyed on an mcp-session-id header.

flow.title: Authenticate, if configured
flow.detail: If OPENCG__MCP__HTTP_TOKEN is set, /mcp requires a matching bearer token. If OPENCG__MCP__OAUTH_PASSWORD is set, an OAuth 2.1 router is mounted so claude.ai can connect as a custom connector. With neither set the endpoint is open and the server logs a warning.

flow.title: Build the pipeline request
flow.detail: For retrieval, the server mints a correlation id, attaches identity from its own configuration, sets tool: "retrieve_for_context", and POSTs to the pipeline's /retrieve with an x-correlation-id header so the two services' logs line up.

flow.title: Return JSON as a text block
flow.detail: MCP results come back as a single text content block containing pretty-printed JSON. Errors return isError: true with a {code, message} payload — for example concept_not_found when traversal is given a bad concept id.

facts: Listens on 8080 in-container, usually mapped to host 8181 (8080 collides on the dev machine)
Connect via stdio docker run, direct HTTP URL, or OAuth for claude.ai
gaps: Three stub tools. search, get_entity, and submit_feedback are advertised but unimplemented, so submit_feedback in particular means no feedback loop exists.
/healthz and /readyz are unauthenticated even when a bearer token is configured.
OAuth is explicitly a stopgap, not a full authorisation-server implementation.
Identity is server-side configuration, not per-caller. Every request from a given server instance carries the same principal, so multi-user attribution is impossible today.

changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

**New model client: `OllamaChat`.** A concrete chat client over the Ollama `/api/chat` shape with `Authorization: Bearer …` support (so it works against Ollama Cloud). The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Vocabulary CRUD.** Admin API to list, add, edit, and deprecate relationship types. The vocabulary table seeds with the seven defaults above; deployments can extend it. Inserts of edges with an unknown vocabulary `type` are rejected at the database level.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns the reachable subgraph as `{nodes, edges}` and includes only `confirmed` edges unless `include_candidates=true` is set.

**MCP `hive_mind/traverse_graph` tool wired up.** The tool's stub returning `not_implemented_in_mvp` is replaced with a real implementation that calls the pipeline's traverse endpoint and returns a structured payload.

**Admin UI graph page at `/graph`.** Three sub-views in one page: (1) a concept browser with filters (`state`, search by name), (2) a concept-detail view showing the concept's confirmed and candidate neighbours, and (3) a candidate review queue ordered by `confidence DESC` with per-row promote / edit / reject actions. **Tabular only — no visual graph rendering in this change.** A small status badge per concept indicates state.
**New shared types:** `Concept`, `ConceptListItem`, `RelationshipType`, `RelationshipEdge`, `EdgeState`, `TraverseRequest`, `TraverseResponse`, `ExtractionResult`.

pillars.title: Admin UI
pillars.tagline: Seven pages, one per layer, so nothing in the system is a black box.
pillars.what: A Next.js 15 application that puts a window on every layer of the stack: what was ingested, what got vectorised, what the graph believes, and what was handed to a model. Each page is a lens on a different pillar.

A retrieval pipeline that cannot be inspected cannot be debugged or trusted. If a search returns nonsense you need to see whether the chunk was bad, the embedding was bad, or the ranking was bad — and those are three different pages.

changes.name: add-ontology-layer
changes.why: The knowledge graph shipped with typed *edges* and untyped *nodes*. `relationship_vocab` constrains the ten legal arrow names, but a `concept` row is just a name, a description, and an aliases array. Nothing records that `parse_config` is a **function**, that `Prompt Caching` is a **topic**, or that `checks.py` is a **module** — and nothing prevents the extractor from emitting `"Prompt Caching" calls "Anthropic API"`, which is meaningless.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: the ontology class.** A named kind of thing (`Function`, `Module`, `Service`, `Topic`, `Document`) with a stable `class_id`, a canonical `name`, a `description`, an optional `parent_class_id`, and a `state` reflecting whether it is part of the seeded core or operator-authored.

**A single-parent subtype hierarchy.** Classes form a tree rooted at `Thing`. Subsumption is transitive: if `Method` is a subtype of `Function` and `Function` is a subtype of `CodeSymbol`, then a `Method` satisfies any constraint written against `CodeSymbol`. Cycles are rejected; a class may not be its own ancestor.

**Concepts gain a class.** `opencg.concept` gains a nullable `class_id` FK. Nullable, not `NOT NULL`, because every concept extracted before this change is genuinely unclassified and pretending otherwise would be a lie in the data. Unclassified concepts sort to the top of the review queue.

**Domain/range constraints on relationship types.** A new table declares which `(domain class, relationship type, range class)` triples are legal — `calls` runs `Function → Function`, `defined_in` runs `CodeSymbol → Module`, `depends_on` runs `Service → Service`. A relationship type with no constraint rows is unconstrained, so existing behaviour is preserved until an operator narrows it.

**The relationship vocabulary is absorbed into the ontology.** `opencg.relationship_vocab` becomes `opencg.ontology_relationship`, and edge types are governed by the ontology's admin API, audit vocabulary, and version rather than by a surface of their own. `name` stays the primary key, so `relationship_edge.type`'s foreign key — and the guarantee that an unknown edge type fails at the database — survives the rename untouched. `/graph/vocab` stays as a deprecated alias for one release. Classes, relationship types, and constraints are one model, versioned together.

**A seeded core ontology, extensible per deployment.** Ships with a small tree covering what openCG actually ingests today — code symbols and documents — plus the constraints for the six code relations graphifyy emits. Operators add classes and constraints through the admin API; nothing about the core is privileged at query time.

**Type-aware extraction.** The prose extractor's prompt is rebuilt from the ontology rather than hardcoded: it names the legal classes, asks the model to classify each concept it emits, and names the legal `(domain, relation, range)` triples instead of a bare list of relation names. The code path classifies deterministically from graphifyy's `symbol_kind`, which already distinguishes `class` / `function` / `method` / `module`.

**Constraint checking is advisory, never fatal.** An edge that violates a constraint is still written, marked `constraint_violation`, and routed to review. It is excluded from traversal by default exactly as a candidate is. Hard database rejection was rejected as an option: it would make a schema edit retroactively destroy extracted data, and it would give ingestion a new way to fail.
**Class-filtered traversal.** `GET /graph/traverse` accepts a `classes` parameter, filtering returned nodes by class with subtype expansion.
**Admin UI `/ontology` page.** A class-tree editor, a constraint matrix per relationship type, and a violations queue. Every ontology edit writes to the existing append-only `graph_audit_log`.

changes.name: add-incremental-ingest
changes.why: Every git re-ingest re-chunks and re-embeds the entire repository. `content_hash` is computed for every file, written to the catalog, and never read back — the only reads are for admin display. Embedding is one sequential HTTP call per chunk, so a repo producing 45,000 chunks pays 45,000 round trips on every run, plus a second model call per prose chunk for graph extraction. Fixing one typo costs the same as the first ingest.
what_changes: **A completion marker replaces the hash as the skip key.** Stored in the parent entity's existing `metadata` JSONB under a namespaced, versioned key, it records the `content_hash` that completed, an `embedding_fingerprint` (provider, model, vector dimension), a `chunker_version` (graphifyy version plus an application-controlled chunker format version and its constants), an `extraction_version`, the `chunk_mode` that was actually used, `chunk_count`, and `completed_at`.

**A file is skipped only when the marker parses, is a known version, and every identity component matches.** Absent, malformed, unknown-version, or any mismatch means process normally. Absent fails open by design: no existing row has a marker, so the first run after this ships reprocesses the corpus once.

**The marker is earned, not assumed.** It is written only after every chunk of that file embedded and upserted without error, extraction was not degraded, the code graph persisted where one was expected, and the file was not truncated mid-flight. Truncation is judged **per file**, not per run.

**The chunker reports why it produced text chunks.** `chunk_code_by_symbols` currently returns plain text chunks from two different places — extraction raised, or the file genuinely has no symbols — with identical return shape. The second is spec-mandated correct behaviour. Without distinguishing them, either degraded files freeze forever or every symbol-free source file reprocesses forever. The function gains an explicit outcome so the marker can tell them apart.

**Marker publication is compare-and-set.** Nothing serialises ingests — every `POST /run/git` spawns a background task — so two runs of the same repo can interleave. The write is conditional on the row still belonging to the attempt that did the work.
**Skipped files are still touched.** A skip bypasses `insert_entity`, so a lightweight catalog method refreshes verification state without rewriting content.

**Markers are invalidatable.** Recreating Qdrant collections is a documented operator procedure, after which every marker still passes and nothing re-ingests. An explicit invalidation path prevents that trap.

**Runs report what they skipped.** `IngestionSummary`, `RunStore`, `GET /runs/recent`, and the admin ingestion page all carry a skipped count. This is a safety surface, not cosmetics: an over-aggressive gate is otherwise invisible.

changes.name: add-foundation
changes.why: General-purpose LLMs are trained on general-purpose knowledge. Enterprise standards, taxonomy, patterns, and policies are specific to each organization and never reach the training data. A single LLM tool RAG-ing against a vector database is one component — not an AI architecture.
what_changes: New service: **MCP server** (TypeScript) exposing `search`, `retrieve_for_context`, `get_entity`, `traverse_graph`, `submit_feedback` tools and a structured response contract.

New service: **Retrieval pipeline** — orchestrates the 7-stage runtime path (identity → intent classification → hybrid retrieval → catalog/graph enrichment → rerank+compress → entitlement+audit → structured return).
New service: **Background enrichment workers** — change-driven enrichment, freshness monitoring, relationship inference, usage-feedback streaming.
New service: **Ingestion connectors** — git, confluence, custom HTTP APIs, and a web-page indexer with allow-listed domains.
New service: **Admin UI** — query review, returned-context inspection, graph relationship management, vector neighbourhood exploration, content management, ingestion control.

New shared storage layer: **PostgreSQL** (Apache AGE for graph, `pg_trgm` and `tsvector` for BM25-style lexical), **Qdrant** (vector store with hybrid dense+sparse), **Valkey** (cache + session), **OPA sidecar** (policy engine).

New abstraction: **Model-provider adapters** — single interface for embeddings, intent classification, rerank, generation; first-class adapters for Ollama and Anthropic; OpenAI-compatible adapter for portability.
**Identity stub** — hardcoded principal + correlation ID in v0; auth is explicitly deferred but the propagation contract is established now so it can be swapped without touching downstream stages.

**Observability built into every stage**: OpenTelemetry traces, Prometheus metrics, and per-stage token accounting (input tokens, output tokens, est. cost, model, latency) on every request, indexed by correlation ID.
**Audit + recreatability** ("SR 26-2") — every assembled context window is logged with retrieved IDs, applied entitlements, model+prompt versions so any decision can be reconstructed.
**Docker Compose** stack with `dev` and `local-prod` profiles for one-command bring-up.

pillars.title: Entitlement and Audit
pillars.tagline: An append-only record of everything ever handed to a model. The database refuses to forget.
pillars.what:
Two things that belong together: the check on who may see what, and the permanent record of what was actually sent.

The audit half is arguably openCG's real differentiator. Most retrieval systems cannot tell you what they fed a model six months ago. This one can reconstruct it exactly.
pillars.why: If a private knowledge base is going to be piped into AI tools, someone will eventually ask what leaked, when, and to whom. Answering that after the fact is impossible unless you wrote it down at the time — so openCG writes a row on every single retrieval, and makes that row physically impossible to alter.

flow.title: Decide what the caller may see
flow.detail: At assemble time each candidate's classification is compared against the classifications its roles allow. admin and reader both get {internal, public}; an unrecognised role gets {public} only. Failing closed on unknown roles is deliberate.

flow.title: Record a verdict per candidate, not just per result
flow.detail: Every candidate the search surfaced gets a decision: include with its token count, deny with classification_restricted, or drop with budget_exhausted. The record shows what was considered and rejected, not only what was returned.

flow.title: Hash the exact assembled context
flow.detail: SHA-256 over the ordered (entity_id, score, text) of the final fragments. Later you can prove whether a given context window is the one that was served.

flow.title: Write one immutable row
flow.detail: Who asked, what they asked, which tool, all candidate ids, all decisions, the final ids, the hash, token counts, latency, outcome, and the model and retriever versions in play — enough to recreate the conditions of the query.

flow.title: Let the database enforce immutability
flow.detail: A trigger on opencg.audit_log blocks DELETE entirely and permits exactly one kind of UPDATE: flipping legal_hold from false to true. This is not a convention the application follows; it is a rule the database enforces against every client, including a human with psql.

flow.title: Partition by time
flow.detail: The table is partitioned by created_at on a weekly cadence with a default partition, so it can grow without the write path degrading.

flow.title: Audit the graph separately
flow.detail: Graph edits get their own append-only table, graph_audit_log, recording actor, target kind, state transition, reason, and full before/after JSONB snapshots. It forbids both UPDATE and DELETE.

flow.title: Read it back
flow.detail: GET /audit/recent and GET /audit/{id} serve the Queries page, and a per-entity lookup finds every audit row whose final set contained a given entity — which is how the entity detail page shows "where this has been used".

changes.name: add-foundation
changes.why: General-purpose LLMs are trained on general-purpose knowledge. Enterprise standards, taxonomy, patterns, and policies are specific to each organization and never reach the training data. A single LLM tool RAG-ing against a vector database is one component — not an AI architecture.
what_changes: New service: **MCP server** (TypeScript) exposing `search`, `retrieve_for_context`, `get_entity`, `traverse_graph`, `submit_feedback` tools and a structured response contract.

New service: **Background enrichment workers** — change-driven enrichment, freshness monitoring, relationship inference, usage-feedback streaming.
New service: **Ingestion connectors** — git, confluence, custom HTTP APIs, and a web-page indexer with allow-listed domains.
New service: **Admin UI** — query review, returned-context inspection, graph relationship management, vector neighbourhood exploration, content management, ingestion control.

changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

**New model client: `OllamaChat`.** A concrete chat client over the Ollama `/api/chat` shape with `Authorization: Bearer …` support (so it works against Ollama Cloud). The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Vocabulary CRUD.** Admin API to list, add, edit, and deprecate relationship types. The vocabulary table seeds with the seven defaults above; deployments can extend it. Inserts of edges with an unknown vocabulary `type` are rejected at the database level.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns the reachable subgraph as `{nodes, edges}` and includes only `confirmed` edges unless `include_candidates=true` is set.

**MCP `hive_mind/traverse_graph` tool wired up.** The tool's stub returning `not_implemented_in_mvp` is replaced with a real implementation that calls the pipeline's traverse endpoint and returns a structured payload.

**Admin UI graph page at `/graph`.** Three sub-views in one page: (1) a concept browser with filters (`state`, search by name), (2) a concept-detail view showing the concept's confirmed and candidate neighbours, and (3) a candidate review queue ordered by `confidence DESC` with per-row promote / edit / reject actions. **Tabular only — no visual graph rendering in this change.** A small status badge per concept indicates state.
**New shared types:** `Concept`, `ConceptListItem`, `RelationshipType`, `RelationshipEdge`, `EdgeState`, `TraverseRequest`, `TraverseResponse`, `ExtractionResult`.

pillars.title: Observability
pillars.tagline: Traces and metrics, with token accounting treated as mandatory.
pillars.what: OpenTelemetry traces plus Prometheus metrics, exported to a collector running in the compose stack. Every pipeline stage opens a span; every model call reports its tokens.
pillars.why:
Two questions need answering continuously. Where did the latency go — which matters because retrieval fans out to several backends and any one of them can be the slow one. And what did this cost — which matters because tokens are the unit of spend, and per-stage attribution is the only way to know which stage to optimise.

The project rules make token reporting non-negotiable: a model call that does not emit a token count is treated as a bug, not an omission.

flow.title: Bootstrap tracing per service
flow.detail: Each service calls setup_otel with its name, which wires an OTLP HTTP exporter pointed at http://otel-collector:4318/v1/traces. Setting the endpoint to none or off disables export cleanly, so tests and offline runs do not need a collector.

flow.title: Span the request and each stage
flow.detail: /retrieve opens pipeline.retrieve with correlation id, tenant, principal, and tool, then child spans per stage. pipeline.hybrid_retrieval carries dense, lexical, and fused counts plus the embedding model; pipeline.assemble carries candidates in, kept, and budget.

flow.title: Count tokens on every model call
flow.detail: record_stage_tokens increments opencg_tokens_total{stage,model,provider,tenant,direction} and the same numbers are set as span attributes. Both the trace and the time series can answer the cost question independently.

flow.title: Count extraction outcomes
flow.detail: Graph extraction emits opencg_extractor_edges_total{relation,state} for edges it produced and opencg_extractor_errors_total{reason} for timeouts, provider failures, and parse failures — which is what makes best-effort extraction observable rather than silent.

flow.title: Expose a scrape endpoint
flow.detail: The pipeline serves Prometheus text at GET /metrics, mounted from the shared metrics app so every service exposes the same registry shape.

flow.title: Return usage in the response too
flow.detail: Beyond telemetry, /retrieve returns a UsageEnvelope with total tokens, latency, and a per-stage breakdown, so a caller sees its own cost without needing access to the metrics backend.

facts: Collector: otel-collector-contrib 0.123.0, OTLP HTTP on 4318, health on 13133
Set the OTLP endpoint to none or off to disable export
gaps: No Grafana, Tempo, Loki, or Prometheus server. The collector receives traces but nothing stores or visualises them; the full stack is specced in add-foundation and deferred.
opencg_stage_latency_seconds is only recorded for graph extraction. Retrieve stages return latency in the response body but never populate the histogram, so stage latency is not queryable over time.
opencg_provider_errors_total is defined but never incremented on the retrieve path.
No structured log aggregation — logs go to stdout and stay there.
No alerting or SLOs.

pillars.title: Deployment and Quality
pillars.tagline: Ten containers, one command, and a smoke test that proves the whole chain works.
pillars.what: The Docker Compose stack that runs everything, plus the testing and process discipline that keeps it honest. make up-d builds and starts ten services; bash tests/smoke/run.sh proves that content can go in one end and come out the other.
pillars.why: openCG's promise is *self-hostable*. That only means something if a single command brings up a working stack on a laptop with no cloud account. flow.title: Build and start the stack
flow.detail: make up-d runs Docker Compose with the dev profile: Postgres, Qdrant, Valkey, Ollama, the OTel collector, then the pipeline, ingestion, MCP server, and admin UI. Every host port is written as ${OPENCG__SERVICE__HOST_PORT:-default} so a collision can be dodged from .env without editing the compose file.

flow.title: Initialise the database in order
flow.detail: Postgres runs its init SQL in numeric order: 010_extensions (AGE, pg_trgm, unaccent, uuid-ossp), 020_catalog, 030_audit, 040_graph, 050_graph_audit, 090_grants. The files start at 010_ specifically so Apache AGE's own bundled 00-create-extension-age.sql runs first.

flow.title: Pull the embedding model on first start
flow.detail: The Ollama container's entrypoint pulls the configured embedding model before reporting healthy, so the first ingest does not fail on a cold model cache.

flow.title: Gate startup on real readiness
flow.detail: Dependent services wait on healthchecks, not just container start. The pipeline waits for Postgres, Qdrant, Valkey, Ollama, and the collector; the MCP server and admin UI wait for the pipeline. Each service's /readyz probes its actual dependencies rather than returning a static OK.

flow.title: Prove the chain end to end
flow.detail: The smoke test ingests a deterministic fixture, retrieves against it, and asserts the whole path — including a stubbed chat service so graph extraction is reproducible instead of depending on a live model. It is bounded and isolated so it can run repeatedly.

flow.title: Keep the spec ahead of the code
flow.detail: Every feature goes through the OpenSpec workflow before implementation: propose, design, write testable WHEN/THEN scenarios, validate --strict, get approval, then build. This explainer's per-pillar history is generated from those documents.

changes.why: The project's final name is **Open Context Graph** (short **openCG**, slug `opencg`). changes.name: fix-symbol-attribution
changes.why: `add-incremental-ingest` gives `chunk_code_by_symbols` a completeness contract: report `symbols` when every discovered symbol produced a chunk, and `partial` when any were lost. A `partial` file never earns a completion marker, so it is reprocessed on the next run rather than skipped — the safety property that stops the gate freezing a half-finished file.
what_changes: **Discovery is narrowed to the nodes the extractor attributed to the file being parsed**, before completeness is judged. A node is kept when its `source_file` resolves to the path handed to `graphify.extract`, and dropped otherwise. That excludes referenced types, whose `source_file` is empty because under single-file extraction their defining file is genuinely unknown, and import targets, whose `source_file` names a different file the extractor never read.

**A malformed definition is kept, not filtered.** A node attributed to this file stays in the discovered population however broken its other fields are, so failing to place it reports as `partial` rather than disappearing. This is why no discriminator-failure guard is needed: the failure mode reports itself.
**A file whose only AST nodes besides the module node were attributed elsewhere** takes the existing zero-symbol path and reports `no_symbols`, so its text is still chunked and searchable.
impact: `services/ingestion/src/opencg_ingestion/chunking.py`: node filtering in `chunk_code_by_symbols`, ahead of the existing module-node filter.
No schema change, no new dependency, no migration, no orphaned rows, no entity-id rotation.

**Sequencing**: must land before `add-incremental-ingest` enables its gate (that change's task 5). It does not block that change's earlier tasks — withholding a marker from a file reporting `partial` is correct behaviour either way, and only the gate turns that into repeated work.

**Archive ordering**: this change MUST NOT be archived before `add-incremental-ingest`. The modified requirement now references that change's *Chunker reports its extraction outcome* by name, and every outcome-asserting scenario here depends on the vocabulary it defines. Archiving first would leave the baseline citing a requirement it does not contain. This change is 27 tasks against that change's 60, so it will plausibly finish first — the constraint is on archiving, not on implementing.

**Pre-existing and out of scope**: in some languages an import statement produces a chunk of its own — `import Foundation` in Swift yields a chunk with `symbol_id = "foundation"`. That node carries both a `source_file` and a `source_location`, so it is indistinguishable from a definition by this change's test and survives unchanged. It is current behaviour, unaffected either way, and belongs to whoever next looks at cross-language chunk quality.

Depends on graphifyy being at or above 0.8.51, already pinned in `services/ingestion/pyproject.toml`. On 0.8.38 the same referenced types additionally stole their function's body, which is a different and worse failure; the version floor closes that and this change closes the accounting.

changes.name: add-ontology-layer
changes.why: The knowledge graph shipped with typed *edges* and untyped *nodes*. `relationship_vocab` constrains the ten legal arrow names, but a `concept` row is just a name, a description, and an aliases array. Nothing records that `parse_config` is a **function**, that `Prompt Caching` is a **topic**, or that `checks.py` is a **module** — and nothing prevents the extractor from emitting `"Prompt Caching" calls "Anthropic API"`, which is meaningless.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: the ontology class.** A named kind of thing (`Function`, `Module`, `Service`, `Topic`, `Document`) with a stable `class_id`, a canonical `name`, a `description`, an optional `parent_class_id`, and a `state` reflecting whether it is part of the seeded core or operator-authored.

**A single-parent subtype hierarchy.** Classes form a tree rooted at `Thing`. Subsumption is transitive: if `Method` is a subtype of `Function` and `Function` is a subtype of `CodeSymbol`, then a `Method` satisfies any constraint written against `CodeSymbol`. Cycles are rejected; a class may not be its own ancestor.

**Concepts gain a class.** `opencg.concept` gains a nullable `class_id` FK. Nullable, not `NOT NULL`, because every concept extracted before this change is genuinely unclassified and pretending otherwise would be a lie in the data. Unclassified concepts sort to the top of the review queue.

**Domain/range constraints on relationship types.** A new table declares which `(domain class, relationship type, range class)` triples are legal — `calls` runs `Function → Function`, `defined_in` runs `CodeSymbol → Module`, `depends_on` runs `Service → Service`. A relationship type with no constraint rows is unconstrained, so existing behaviour is preserved until an operator narrows it.

**The relationship vocabulary is absorbed into the ontology.** `opencg.relationship_vocab` becomes `opencg.ontology_relationship`, and edge types are governed by the ontology's admin API, audit vocabulary, and version rather than by a surface of their own. `name` stays the primary key, so `relationship_edge.type`'s foreign key — and the guarantee that an unknown edge type fails at the database — survives the rename untouched. `/graph/vocab` stays as a deprecated alias for one release. Classes, relationship types, and constraints are one model, versioned together.

**A seeded core ontology, extensible per deployment.** Ships with a small tree covering what openCG actually ingests today — code symbols and documents — plus the constraints for the six code relations graphifyy emits. Operators add classes and constraints through the admin API; nothing about the core is privileged at query time.

**Type-aware extraction.** The prose extractor's prompt is rebuilt from the ontology rather than hardcoded: it names the legal classes, asks the model to classify each concept it emits, and names the legal `(domain, relation, range)` triples instead of a bare list of relation names. The code path classifies deterministically from graphifyy's `symbol_kind`, which already distinguishes `class` / `function` / `method` / `module`.

**Constraint checking is advisory, never fatal.** An edge that violates a constraint is still written, marked `constraint_violation`, and routed to review. It is excluded from traversal by default exactly as a candidate is. Hard database rejection was rejected as an option: it would make a schema edit retroactively destroy extracted data, and it would give ingestion a new way to fail.
**Class-filtered traversal.** `GET /graph/traverse` accepts a `classes` parameter, filtering returned nodes by class with subtype expansion.
**Admin UI `/ontology` page.** A class-tree editor, a constraint matrix per relationship type, and a violations queue. Every ontology edit writes to the existing append-only `graph_audit_log`.

changes.name: add-incremental-ingest
changes.why: Every git re-ingest re-chunks and re-embeds the entire repository. `content_hash` is computed for every file, written to the catalog, and never read back — the only reads are for admin display. Embedding is one sequential HTTP call per chunk, so a repo producing 45,000 chunks pays 45,000 round trips on every run, plus a second model call per prose chunk for graph extraction. Fixing one typo costs the same as the first ingest.
what_changes: **A completion marker replaces the hash as the skip key.** Stored in the parent entity's existing `metadata` JSONB under a namespaced, versioned key, it records the `content_hash` that completed, an `embedding_fingerprint` (provider, model, vector dimension), a `chunker_version` (graphifyy version plus an application-controlled chunker format version and its constants), an `extraction_version`, the `chunk_mode` that was actually used, `chunk_count`, and `completed_at`.

**A file is skipped only when the marker parses, is a known version, and every identity component matches.** Absent, malformed, unknown-version, or any mismatch means process normally. Absent fails open by design: no existing row has a marker, so the first run after this ships reprocesses the corpus once.

**The marker is earned, not assumed.** It is written only after every chunk of that file embedded and upserted without error, extraction was not degraded, the code graph persisted where one was expected, and the file was not truncated mid-flight. Truncation is judged **per file**, not per run.

**The chunker reports why it produced text chunks.** `chunk_code_by_symbols` currently returns plain text chunks from two different places — extraction raised, or the file genuinely has no symbols — with identical return shape. The second is spec-mandated correct behaviour. Without distinguishing them, either degraded files freeze forever or every symbol-free source file reprocesses forever. The function gains an explicit outcome so the marker can tell them apart.

**Marker publication is compare-and-set.** Nothing serialises ingests — every `POST /run/git` spawns a background task — so two runs of the same repo can interleave. The write is conditional on the row still belonging to the attempt that did the work.
**Skipped files are still touched.** A skip bypasses `insert_entity`, so a lightweight catalog method refreshes verification state without rewriting content.

**Markers are invalidatable.** Recreating Qdrant collections is a documented operator procedure, after which every marker still passes and nothing re-ingests. An explicit invalidation path prevents that trap.

**Runs report what they skipped.** `IngestionSummary`, `RunStore`, `GET /runs/recent`, and the admin ingestion page all carry a skipped count. This is a safety surface, not cosmetics: an over-aggressive gate is otherwise invisible.
impact: **No new column, but one new index.** The marker lives in the existing `metadata JSONB`, deliberately avoiding the absent migration tooling — init SQL runs only against an empty data directory. The set-based chunk refresh does require an index on `opencg.entity (tenant, parent_entity_id)`, which Postgres does not create for a foreign key automatically. An index is not part of the data contract — its absence degrades speed, not correctness — and it can be added to a live database with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`. It is also already owed: `get_entity_with_lineage` sequentially scans on that column today.
`services/ingestion/src/opencg_ingestion/chunking.py`: `chunk_code_by_symbols` gains an outcome in its return.
`services/ingestion/src/opencg_ingestion/pipeline_runner.py`: the gate at the top of the document loop, per-file success and degradation tracking, the marker write after the chunk loop.

`services/pipeline/src/opencg_pipeline/storage/catalog.py`: three new methods. `infra/postgres/init/020_catalog.sql` gains the index, with the `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` equivalent documented in `docs/OPERATIONS.md` for existing databases.

`services/ingestion/src/opencg_ingestion/runs.py`, `server.py`, `cli.py`: skipped counts. Note `IngestionSummary.__iter__` yields exactly two values and `server.py` unpacks it — a third value breaks HTTP-triggered ingests only, invisible to the CLI and the smoke.
`packages/shared` and `packages/shared-py`: `skipped` on `IngestionRun`.
`services/admin-ui`: `IngestionRunRow.tsx` plus its mandatory `*.stories.tsx` neighbour, and the grid header in `app/ingestion/page.tsx`.
`tests/smoke/run.sh`: a second-ingest assertion block, placed before the existing tombstone step, leaving the current assertions untouched.
`tools/explainer/content/01-ingestion.md`: its gap list names "No unchanged-content short-circuit" by name.

**Interaction with `add-ontology-layer`.** That change defers backfilling unclassified concepts, which is only safe while re-ingest redoes everything and picks up new classifications for free. This change removes that. The marker therefore carries an `extraction_version` so an ontology or extractor change invalidates it. The two changes should not be implemented concurrently — both touch code around the graph writer.

**Two operator-visible behaviour shifts, both improvements, both silent.** `updated_at` is deliberately not bumped on a skip, so the `/entities` browser reorders from "most recently ingested" — arbitrary within a run, since every row shared a timestamp — to "most recently changed". And `re-extract --since`, which filters on that column, starts selecting only genuinely changed content instead of nearly everything ingested after the date. Both are captured as spec scenarios so they are tested rather than discovered as bugs.

**Operator deletions start sticking.** `insert_entity` clears `tombstoned_at` unconditionally, so re-ingest currently revives anything an admin tombstoned. A skipped file no longer does. Better behaviour, adopted deliberately rather than inherited.
**Operator-visible one-off**: the first run after this ships reprocesses the whole corpus, which also repairs any file left incomplete by a past interrupted run. Documented in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

**`bootstrap-thin-mvp` is not repaired here.** Four of its six ingestion `MODIFIED` blocks target requirements that exist only in the unarchived `add-foundation` and are absent from the baseline, so it cannot be archived cleanly — and `openspec validate --strict` passes on it today without warning. One of those four also contradicts this change. Recorded as a follow-up rather than fixed from inside this one.

The git connector curates 35 file extensions and 9 skip-dirs in a Python set; the chunker splits on `\n\n` paragraph boundaries. For markdown and prose that's fine. changes.name: add-knowledge-graph
changes.why: The original product brief asked for relationships between *concepts* — "we want to be able to name relationships for how concepts are related to each other. We need a way to do this automatically and then review and edit through an admin interface." Today the catalogue is a flat bag of documents and chunks. Vector search finds what's semantically close; the lexical leg finds what shares vocabulary; neither answers "what's connected, and how." That is exactly the gap `add-foundation`'s `knowledge-graph` capability promised to fill, and that `bootstrap-thin-mvp` deferred.
what_changes: **New first-class entity: `concept`.** Concepts are the nodes of the knowledge graph and are distinct from catalog `entity` rows (which are files / chunks). A concept has a stable `concept_id`, a canonical `name`, a normalised dedupe key, an optional `description`, an `aliases` array, and a `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`). Concepts are stored in a Postgres table; the Apache AGE graph that's already loaded becomes the home for edges.

**New edge model: typed, audited relationships between concepts.** Edges are typed from a curated **vocabulary** (a small extensible table seeded with `depends_on`, `defined_in`, `supersedes`, `mentions`, `related_to`, `causes`, `derived_from`). Every edge carries `state` (`candidate` / `confirmed`), `confidence`, `evidence_uri` (pointing at the source chunk), `extractor_version`, and timestamps. Candidate edges MUST NOT appear in traversal results by default.

**Automatic extraction during ingestion.** When the git connector finishes upserting a chunk, the ingestion pipeline runs a *concept-and-relationship extractor* against that chunk's text using a chat model. The extractor emits a list of `{concept_a, relation, concept_b, evidence_span, confidence}` triples. Concepts are deduped by a normalised name key (Unicode-folded, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). New concepts AND new edges land in `candidate` state.

**New model client: `OllamaChat`.** A concrete chat client over the Ollama `/api/chat` shape with `Authorization: Bearer …` support (so it works against Ollama Cloud). The thin MVP got away with one model caller (embeddings); we now have two. To avoid premature abstraction we ship two concrete clients (`OllamaEmbeddings` + `OllamaChat`) plus a single shared `ProviderConfig` that selects per-capability `(provider, model, base_url, api_key)`. The full provider-protocol abstraction described in `add-foundation/specs/model-providers/spec.md` is still deferred until a *third* caller exists.

**Vocabulary CRUD.** Admin API to list, add, edit, and deprecate relationship types. The vocabulary table seeds with the seven defaults above; deployments can extend it. Inserts of edges with an unknown vocabulary `type` are rejected at the database level.

**Candidate review workflow.** Admin API and UI for browsing candidate concepts and edges, promoting them to `confirmed`, editing their type or endpoints, or deleting them. Every state transition writes an audit row (separate from the retrieval audit log) capturing actor, before, after, and reason.

**`GET /graph/concepts` / `GET /graph/concepts/{id}` / `GET /graph/traverse`** read endpoints on the pipeline service, plus the corresponding admin write endpoints. `traverse` accepts a starting `concept_id`, an optional list of relationship `types`, a `depth` (default 2, max 4), and a result `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns the reachable subgraph as `{nodes, edges}` and includes only `confirmed` edges unless `include_candidates=true` is set.

**MCP `hive_mind/traverse_graph` tool wired up.** The tool's stub returning `not_implemented_in_mvp` is replaced with a real implementation that calls the pipeline's traverse endpoint and returns a structured payload.

**Admin UI graph page at `/graph`.** Three sub-views in one page: (1) a concept browser with filters (`state`, search by name), (2) a concept-detail view showing the concept's confirmed and candidate neighbours, and (3) a candidate review queue ordered by `confidence DESC` with per-row promote / edit / reject actions. **Tabular only — no visual graph rendering in this change.** A small status badge per concept indicates state.

changes.name: add-admin-vector-and-content
changes.why: The thin MVP gave operators a query review surface, but the user explicitly asked for an admin interface that also covers **vector search**, **review and management of content**, and **adding content**. Today the only way to see what's in the catalogue is to write SQL or curl Qdrant directly. That is fine for engineers, useless for operators, and makes the catalogue feel like a black box — which is the opposite of the architectural promise.
what_changes: New admin UI pages: - `/vectors` — vector search by free-text query, returning the top-K nearest catalog entities with score, source, classification, and a snippet. Drill-in shows the entity's nearest neighbours. - `/entities` — filterable, paginated entity browser (by source, classification, freshness). - `/entities/[id]` — entity detail: raw text, lineage (parent + chunks), source URI, metadata, freshness, recent audit appearances. Tombstone action. - `/ingestion` — configured connectors with last-run / next-run / error-count / status, plus a "Run now" panel that triggers a git ingest with a user-supplied URL.

New pipeline read endpoints (HTTP, JSON): - `GET /entities?source&classification&freshness_state&limit&offset` — list. - `GET /entities/{id}` — single entity with lineage children/parent. - `POST /search/vector` — `{query, top_k, filters?}` → ordered hits with `entity_id`, `score`, `payload`. Uses the same embeddings client the retrieval path uses; emits its own OTel span + token counter increment. - `DELETE /entities/{id}` — tombstone (sets `tombstoned_at`; cascades none). - `GET /ingestion/connectors` — connector list (proxies the ingestion service). - `POST /ingestion/git/run` — `{repo_url}` (proxies the ingestion service). - `GET /ingestion/runs/recent` — recent runs (proxies the ingestion service).

New ingestion HTTP surface (FastAPI, exposed inside the compose network only): - `POST /run/git` — kick off an ingest in a background task; return `{run_id, status:"queued"}`. - `GET /runs/recent` — in-memory list of recent runs (id, repo, started_at, finished_at, status, parents, chunks, error). - `GET /connectors` — `[{name: "git", supported: true}, ...]` mirroring the v0 capability set.
Shared types added to `packages/shared` and `packages/shared-py`: `Entity`, `EntityListItem`, `VectorSearchHit`, `IngestionRun`, `ConnectorStatus`.
New Storybook stories for every new component (`EntityRow`, `EntityDetail`, `VectorHit`, `ConnectorCard`, `IngestionRunRow`).
Vitest unit tests for every new admin UI component and the new pipeline endpoints (respx + httpx test client for the new routes; the existing patterns generalise).
impact: `services/admin-ui` gains four pages, ~half a dozen components, and matching stories + tests.

`services/pipeline` gains six new routes, a vector-search code path that mirrors stage 3 of the runtime pipeline but is **standalone** (no audit row written — vector search is exploration, not an audited retrieval).

`services/ingestion` becomes a long-running HTTP server in addition to a CLI. Its Dockerfile gains a `CMD ["uv","run","--package","hive-mind-ingestion","uvicorn", ...]`. The CLI binary keeps working unchanged.
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: `ingestion` gains a port mapping (`8100:8100`) and a healthcheck against `/healthz`.
No new external dependencies (no new images, no new model calls).

No new MCP tools and no spec changes to `mcp-server`. Vector search is admin-only because exposing it as an MCP tool without audit-side-effects breaks the recreatability story for `retrieve_for_context`. If we later want an MCP `search` tool, that's its own change with its own audit semantics.
